# Fidelity sweep — oracle correctness gate

`test/check.py` only proves **determinism** (the port renders the same bytes as
its own stored sha256 baselines). It can NOT tell whether those bytes are
*correct* — the baselines were generated by the port itself, with
`V2_RONAN=OFF`. That blind spot hid a real bug: with `V2_RONAN=ON` the
channel-15 → Ronan routing silenced fr08's ch15 music from 1:58, and the
determinism gate stayed green the whole time.

This sweep is the missing **correctness** check: render each corpus song through
its *genuine period engine* (the demo's own V2, extracted from the shipping
binary) and through the port, then compare. A divergence here is a real
fidelity regression.

## Run

    cmake -S . -B build -DV2_RONAN=ON          # speech songs need Ronan in
    cmake --build build --target v2redux
    python3 fidelity/sweep.py                  # nonzero exit if any song fails

Expected (2026-06-22, after the ch15 fix):

| song | era | corr | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| fr08 | v0 | ~1.0 (bit-exact) | the ch15 fix |
| flybye | v1 | ~1.0 (bit-exact) | |
| fr014 | v3 | 0.99989 | documented solved level |
| fr019 | v4 | ~1.0 | ε-floor |
| candytron | v5 | ~0.9997 | known Ronan aspiration-noise residual |
| kkrieger | v5 | 0.99998 | rendered with the `kkrieger2004` era (FM float); under Auto it diverges (known, format-ungateable FM-phase issue) |

Requirements: a 32-bit runtime for the oracle harnesses (`gcc-multilib` /
`lib32-glibc`), Python 3.

## Vendored binaries (gitignored)

`images/<song>.bin` — the depacked period demo image (loaded at base 0x400000).
`oracles/<song>` — the oracle harness that drives that image's genuine 2000-2004
synth. Both are third-party demo code → **not committed**, but fully regenerable.

### Regenerate the images

The depack is static (no Wine) via the `era` toolkit. Source demo .exe files
live in `~/downloads/` (provenance: `fr_public/v2/v2m/era-hunt-manifest.md`);
candytron/kkrieger images are also in their `fr_public/v2/v2m/*-extraction/`
dirs.

    ERA=…/fr_public/v2/v2m/toolkit/era
    unzip -o ~/downloads/fr08_final.zip   # -> fr08v101.exe
    $ERA unpack fr08v101.exe fidelity/images/fr08.bin     # md5 2c1ebe7e…
    # flybye=fr013_unoff.zip, fr014.zip, fr019_party.zip similarly

| song | image src | source zip (~/downloads) |
|---|---|---|
| fr08 | era unpack | fr08_final.zip (fr08v101.exe) |
| flybye | era unpack | fr013_unoff.zip (flybye.exe) |
| fr014 | era unpack | fr014.zip (mark&sweep.exe) |
| fr019 | era unpack | fr019_party.zip (fr-019-party-b.exe) |
| candytron | copy | fr_public/.../candytron-extraction/unpacked.bin |
| kkrieger | copy | fr_public/.../kkrieger-extraction/unpacked_fixed.bin |

### Regenerate the harnesses

Sources live in `fr_public/v2/v2m/<song>-extraction/` (and
`fr_public/v2/validate/c1_fr08_harness.c`). All 32-bit, no-pie:

    gcc -m32 -no-pie -O0 c1_fr08_harness.c -o fidelity/oracles/c1_fr08
    # flybye/fr014/fr019 the same; candytron c2_oracle.c, kkrieger oracle.

Harness invocation styles (encoded in sweep.py): the `c1_*` harnesses carve the
v2m embedded in the image (`<harness> <image> <out.f32> <chunk> <secs>`);
`c2_candytron` and `kkrieger` take a v2m argument
(`<harness> <image> <v2m> <out.f32> <secs>`).
